ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A rectangular coil with resistance 1 Ω rotates at a constant speed in a uniform magnetic field around an axis perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, and the image of the alternating electromotive force produced changing with time is as shown in the figure. Now this alternating current is applied to an electric heating wire with resistance 9 Ω. What is the heating power of the electric heating wire?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The heating power of the electric heating wire at this time is P＝1 800 W
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a sinusoidal curve of alternating electromotive force u changing with time t, the vertical axis is labeled u/V, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s. The maximum value of the curve is +200 V, and the minimum value is -200 V; the figure also marks that it reaches the positive peak value 200 V near t=0.01 s, and reaches the negative peak value -200 V near t=0.02 s. From this, the peak value of the alternating electromotive force can be read as Em=200 V. Reasoning calculation: The coil's own resistance is r=1 Ω, and the resistance of the externally connected electric heating wire is R=9 Ω. The effective electromotive force of the sinusoidal alternating current is E=Em/√2=200/√2 V. After connecting the electric heating wire, the total resistance of the circuit is r+R=1+9=10 Ω, so the effective current is I=E/(r+R)=(200/√2)/10=10√2 A. The heating power of the electric heating wire is P=I²R=(10√2)²×9=200×9=1800 W.
